question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, military, and key institutions continues to underpin trader expectations that he will remain in power through at least the 21st Party Congress in 2027. With no designated successor and recent personnel decisions plus policy continuity at plenums and National People's Congress sessions through mid-2026, elite consensus appears stable despite occasional unverified health speculation. The 95.3% implied probability on "No" reflects this structural reality and absence of credible removal triggers. Realistic shifts could still arise from sudden health developments, major elite realignments ahead of the congress, or unforeseen external shocks altering internal dynamics.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains wide open more than two years before the first contests, with no major candidate having declared and early positioning still fluid following the 2024 cycle. This keeps implied probabilities tightly clustered among Gavin Newsom, Jon Ossoff, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez because voter coalitions, fundraising networks, and early-state dynamics have not yet consolidated. Ossoff’s recent rise reflects growing attention to his Senate profile in Georgia and appeal as a younger, battleground-state figure, while Newsom benefits from California executive experience and national visibility. Ocasio-Cortez draws consistent progressive support, as seen in New Hampshire polling. Democrats’ July 2026 decision to open the nominating calendar in South Carolina further underscores the emphasis on diverse voter bases. Separation could emerge from formal announcements, stronger polling aggregates, endorsements from party leaders, or standout midterm performances that shift trader assessments of general-election viability.

This keeps implied probabilities tightly clustered among Gavin Newsom, Jon Ossoff, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez because voter coalitions, fundraising networks, and early-state dynamics have not yet consolidated. Ossoff’s recent rise reflects growing attention to his Senate profile in Georgia and appeal as a younger, battleground-state figure, while Newsom benefits from California executive experience and national visibility. Ocasio-Cortez draws consistent progressive support, as seen in New Hampshire polling. Democrats’ July 2026 decision to open the nominating calendar in South Carolina further underscores the emphasis on diverse voter bases. Separation could emerge from formal announcements, stronger polling aggregates, endorsements from party leaders, or standout midterm performances that shift trader assessments of general-election viability.
